record.paper_title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
record.original_question: For planar systems of the form ẋ = P_{2k+1}(x,y), ẏ = Q_{2ℓ+1}(x,y), where P_{2k+1} and Q_{2ℓ+1} are homogeneous polynomials of odd degrees 2k+1 and 2ℓ+1, characterize exactly which such systems have a center at the origin.

evidence.quote: Problem 13. (i) Characterize the centers of the above family.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider planar polynomial differential systems of the form
    ẋ = P(x,y),    ẏ = Q(x,y),
where P and Q are real homogeneous polynomials of odd degrees 2k+1 and 2ℓ+1, respectively, with k, ℓ ≥ 0. Recall that the origin is a center of such a system if it is a singular point with a punctured neighborhood entirely filled by periodic orbits surrounding it.

Give a complete characterization (in terms of explicit algebraic conditions on the coefficients of P and Q) of those pairs (P, Q) of homogeneous polynomials of odd degrees 2k+1 and 2ℓ+1 for which the associated planar system has a center at the origin.
artifact.category_tag: centers of planar polynomial vector fields
artifact.status_search_result: For the special case k = ℓ (both components homogeneous of the same odd degree) and for quasi-homogeneous variants, there are known characterizations of centers in the literature. However, no general explicit characterization of centers for arbitrary pairs of homogeneous polynomials of (possibly different) odd degrees 2k+1 and 2ℓ+1 appears to be available; partial results exist for low degrees and for quasi-homogeneous cases, but the general problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Centers of quasi-homogeneous polynomial planar systems
status_evidence.snippet: Necessary and sufficient conditions for a quasi-homogeneous polynomial system of odd degree to have a center are obtained, while no centers exist for even degree.
status_evidence.claim: Center conditions are known in the quasi-homogeneous setting but not in the general non-quasi-homogeneous mixed odd-degree case treated here.

status_evidence.title: On the center criterion of planar quasi-homogeneous polynomial differential systems
status_evidence.snippet: Center criteria are developed for quasi-homogeneous polynomial differential systems.
status_evidence.claim: Available characterizations cover quasi-homogeneous subclasses, leaving the general two-odd-degree homogeneous case open.
